title: Minimum shelf life at arrival
notes: WHO, Guidelines for medicine donations, revised 2010 (ISBN 978 92 4 150198 9), Article 6: 'After arrival in the recipient country all donated medicines should have a remaining shelf-life of at least one year.' Read by Claude on 2026-11-12 from the publication page and its PDF (SHA-256 cb41c017c38714425150f3e82f7d12b72667ae3c5192207b996723dc088cb89b). One year is counted as 365 days from the arrival date, and exactly 365 days passes (owner, 2026-11-12; OD-009, ADR-013). The same article allows two exceptions, neither applied here: direct donations to a specific health facility whose staff know the shelf life is limited and can use the stock before expiry; and medicines with a total shelf life under two years, of which at least one third, and at least six months, should remain (OD-053). Placeholder until a pharmacist or clinician checks it (OD-002).
